solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cut back on depleted uranium, importing one radioactive metal

indicators.note: importing says the whole string takes the letter for one inside it
back says the word for cut is read in reverse
depleted says the word uranium is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An instruction to reduce use of depleted uranium while bringing in another radioactive element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LOP into POL; 'depleted' empties uranium to UM; 'importing' puts I into POLONUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Polonium is a highly radioactive chemical element discovered by Marie Curie, a metal by classification.

clue.text: The last time doctor turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up says the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: The final appointment before the doctor finally arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses AGEMO in this down entry. Doctor as MO (Medical Officer) is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the end or the final one of anything.

clue.text: Arrange the score Mozart half abandoned?

indicators.note: abandoned, in the sense of wild and unrestrained, signals that these letters are mixed up
half says only one half of the word Mozart is used, here its second half

explanation.surface: Wondering whether one might arrange a Mozart score with half of it thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps ART from Mozart, and 'abandoned' shuffles THE SCORE ART. The musical surface makes the definition apt.
explanation.definitionFit: To orchestrate is to arrange music for an orchestra, and more broadly to organise or arrange anything.

clue.text: One following boxing representative around is amateur

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: boxing says the word for following encloses the other piece
around says the short word for representative is turned round

explanation.surface: A sporting remark that someone who trails a boxing representative is no professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the representative backwards, and 'boxing' sets that inside the word for following. 'boxing' looks like the sport but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inexpert lacks skill, like an amateur as opposed to a professional.

clue.text: After distance driven carrying theologian, padre's changing spare tyre

indicators.note: After says the first part comes before the shuffled clergyman's letters
carrying says the word for distance driven holds the theologian's letters

parts.note: mileage is the distance a vehicle has been driven
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

indicators.note: changing says the letters of padre's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A motoring scene: a clergyman changing a spare tyre after a long drive with a theologian aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' and 'changing' are the container and anagram signals. 'spare tyre' looks like car talk but is the roll of fat round the waist; DD (Doctor of Divinity) is the usual theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare tyre is jocular slang for a roll of fat round the waist, the thickening that comes with middle years.

clue.text: Small children with the same pop group?

definitions.note: a singular word defining a plural answer; the answer means bands or teams

parts.note: quads are quadruplets, children who share one father, or pop

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about young children all fans of the same pop band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' looks like pop music but is Dad: quadruplets share one.
explanation.definitionFit: Squads are small organised teams or bodies of people, such as sports teams or army units.

clue.text: Most sensible, wanting home in Jo'burg?

parts.note: Johannesburg, Jo'burg for short, is in South Africa, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Asks whether the wisest choice is to want a house in Johannesburg.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, a home in Jo'burg is a South African nest: SA plus NEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of sane, meaning the most rational or level-headed.

clue.text: Embrace top to bottom? That's disgusting!

indicators.note: in a down entry, top to bottom says the first letter is taken from the top and put at the foot

explanation.surface: Someone recoiling from a full-length hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top to bottom' moves the H of HUG from the top to the bottom of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugh is an exclamation of revulsion or disgust.

clue.text: Describe English river rising in time

indicators.note: in says the reversed letters go inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising says these letters read upwards

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river

explanation.surface: Asks for an account of an English river swelling in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ENILE into ELINE, and 'in' puts it inside DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To delineate is to portray or set out in detail, so to describe precisely.

clue.text: Fellow heading off to deliver grass

indicators.note: heading off says the word for deliver loses its first letter

parts.note: to rescue is to deliver from danger

explanation.surface: A man setting off to deliver some grass, perhaps of the smokable kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the R of RESCUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fescue is a kind of grass common in lawns and pasture.

clue.text: Hung out in Herb's squalid place

indicators.note: in says the shuffled letters go inside the herb

parts.note: dill is a herb; the 's is read as is

indicators.note: out, as in out of order, says the letters of hung are rearranged

explanation.surface: Herb, a person, has a grimy home where something was hung out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a man's name but is the plant; 'out' shuffles the four letters of hung to UNGH, and 'in' sets them inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunghill is a heap of manure, figuratively any filthy, degraded place.

clue.text: Come to trail

definitions.meaning: to come to is to regain consciousness, to rouse from sleep
the track left behind a moving ship

explanation.definitionFit: Waking means regaining consciousness; a ship's wake is the trail of disturbed water behind it.

clue.text: Lightest rain troubled Italian composer

indicators.note: troubled says the letters of rain are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A light drizzle bothered an Italian composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lightest' suggests weight but means palest in shade; 'troubled' shuffles RAIN to RINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina was the great Italian Renaissance composer of church music.

clue.text: Breathing fresh air in port's exhilarating initially

indicators.note: fresh, meaning new, signals that the letters are made into a new order
initially says only the opening letter of exhilarating is used

explanation.surface: A seaside observation that breathing fresh air at the port is exhilarating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the opening letter of exhilarating, and 'fresh' shuffles everything else with it. 'fresh air' reads as one phrase but splits into signal and letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Respiration is the process of breathing in and out.

clue.text: Incline, with age, to catch one disease

parts.note: a ship's list is an incline or lean

indicators.note: to catch says the word for age holds the letter for one

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Suggests that getting older makes one inclined to pick up an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' puts I inside ERA. 'catch' sits well with disease but works as the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Listeriosis is a food-borne infection caused by Listeria bacteria; the bacterium's name serves for the illness.

clue.text: Not living at home, Australian turned up in China

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up says the little word in reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
china is rhyming slang for mate, from china plate

explanation.surface: Someone no longer living at home: an Aussie who has turned up in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses IN to NI. 'China' looks like the country but is the rhyming slang: china plate = mate, a Cockney London expression for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanimate means lifeless, lacking the qualities of a living being.

clue.text: Son needs taxi? He won't come out

explanation.surface: A son needs a taxi because some man refuses to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come out' means strike: a scab is a worker who refuses to join a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is a strikebreaker, someone who keeps working when colleagues walk out.

clue.text: Tops second of pizzas with pepper

indicators.note: second of says the second letter of pizzas is taken

parts.note: cum is Latin for with, as in a bed-cum-sofa

explanation.surface: A pizza order: the second pizza topped with peppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second of' picks I, the second letter of pizzas. CUM is Latin for 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsicum is the genus of sweet and chilli peppers, and the usual name for the vegetable in many countries.

clue.text: Drink is knocked back by a prince

indicators.note: knocked back says the word for a drink is turned backwards

parts.note: a jar is a drink, especially of beer

explanation.surface: A prince knocks back a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like downing a drink but reverses JAR to RAJ. 'Jar' is British slang for a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A raja is an Indian prince or king.

clue.text: Investigates a Ximenes cryptic

indicators.note: cryptic, meaning obscure or concealed, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone studying a puzzle by Ximenes, the celebrated crossword setter.
explanation.walkthrough: Ximenes was the pseudonym of D. S. Macnutt, the Observer setter whose rules govern fair cryptic clues; 'cryptic' shuffles A XIMENES.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine is to inspect or look into closely.

clue.text: A short time to wear out clothes

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to tire is to wear out

explanation.surface: A brief spell in which to wear out one's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wear' sits naturally beside clothes but belongs with 'out' as TIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Attire means clothing or dress.

clue.text: Recordings of a TV episode broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast, meaning scattered, signals the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Recordings made of a television episode when it was broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' fits the TV scene but scatters A TV EPISODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Videotapes are magnetic tapes holding recorded TV pictures and sound.

clue.text: She features in American newspaper

indicators.note: features says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman appears in an American newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is the definition: the answer is any woman's name, here found across 'AmericAN NEwspaper'.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, standing for any woman referred to as she.

clue.text: Attack when upset, making remarks

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset says the phrase is turned upside down, so read upwards

parts.note: to set on someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: Someone making remarks when an attack goes badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an anagram signal but reverses SET ON in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes are brief written comments or observations.

clue.text: Standard place to keep a sponge

indicators.note: to keep says the standard and the place hold the a between them

parts.note: par is the normal standard, as on a golf hole

explanation.surface: Looks like advice on the usual place to store a bath sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sponge' looks like the bath item but means a person who sponges off others.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponger lives off others, just as a parasite feeds on its host.

clue.text: Lawyer regularly visited northern town

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of lawyer is taken, here the even ones

explanation.surface: A lawyer making regular visits to a town in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland, hence northern from the British view.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a Scottish seaside town, so in the north of Britain.

clue.text: Material, a small amount found in Czech Republic

indicators.note: found in says the small amount sits inside the country's code

parts.note: CZ is the international code for the Czech Republic
a hint is a small amount, a trace

explanation.surface: A little fabric discovered in the Czech Republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is the container signal; 'a small amount' must be taken whole, article included, to give the inner piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Chintz is a glazed cotton fabric printed with flowery patterns.

clue.text: Picks up European car for final journey

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it

explanation.surface: Someone collecting a European car for one last drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picks up' suggests collecting a car but means hears.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is the vehicle carrying a coffin to a funeral, a body's last trip.

clue.text: Make less food, eating little

indicators.note: eating says the word for food swallows the word for little

parts.note: a dish is food prepared for serving

explanation.surface: Advice to cut down on food by eating only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' looks part of the diet advice but is the container signal, with the food swallowing the little word.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish is to reduce or lessen something.
